info.title: REST API (/v1)
info.description: A thin HTTP adapter for programmatic access to collections, governed by the same broker that powers the MCP server and web UI.

tags.name: acl
tags.description: Per-document access control. Authorised against the caller's standing, not a grant.

tags.name: proposals
tags.description: Deciding on a pending write. There is deliberately no GET /v1/proposals/{id} — reviewing a proposal's proposed content is a console-only surface, not part of this public commitment.

post.summary: Run up to MAX_BATCH_QUERIES labelled queries in one request

requestBody.description: Each entry is a QueryIntent plus a caller-chosen `label` used to key its slot in the response. Sub-queries run sequentially and are independently grant-checked; a refusing sub-query returns its own reason in its slot and does not change the HTTP status — the envelope succeeds as long as the request itself was well-formed.

200.description: One result (or refusal) per label, in the same shape POST /query returns.

post.summary: Structured query: filters, ordering, aggregation, grouping

requestBody.description: The collection comes from the path, never the body. `after` takes a previous response's `nextCursor` for a stable keyset walk and is mutually exclusive with `offset` and `aggregate`.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Repeatable. Fields to return; defaults to every granted field.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Capped, not rejected: default 100, max 500. An oversized limit succeeds and is clamped.

200.description: select * from app.grants for this caller, plus computed effectiveStatus/collectionType/taxonomyFields. additionalProperties is open on purpose — see docs/rest-api.md known warts.

post.summary: Decide on a batch of proposals atomically

requestBody.description: Up to MAX_BATCH_DECISIONS decisions, each an independent approve or reject. Either every one of them commits or none does — the first refusal rolls the whole batch back.

200.description: Every decision in the batch committed.
